filters.addDetail: Every report keeps only the visits that match, until the filter is removed.
filters.valueHint: Pick one of this period's values or type another; (none) is a visit without one.
filters.patternHint: Pick one of this period's values or type another; * matches any characters, such as /blog/*.

segments.name: Name
segments.shareDetail: Off: only you see it in the segment list.

channelHow.ai: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or another assistant refers the visit, or utm_source names one
channelHow.paid-search: A search engine with utm_medium cpc, ppc or paid, or an ad click id such as gclid
channelHow.organic-search: A search engine refers the visit and nothing says it was paid
channelHow.paid-social: A social network with a paid utm_medium or an ad click id
channelHow.social: A social network refers the visit, or utm_medium is social
channelHow.email: utm_medium or utm_source is email or newsletter, or a webmail refers the visit
channelHow.display: utm_medium is display, banner, cpm or another display medium
channelHow.paid-other: Paid by utm_medium or an ad click id, from anywhere else
channelHow.referral: Any other site links to the page
channelHow.other: utm_* parameters without a referrer that fit no other channel
channelHow.direct: No referrer and no utm_* parameters

report.failed: The report could not be loaded
report.nothingYetDetail: Once the site's script is on its pages, visits show here within seconds.

table.engagedDetail: Stayed longer than 10 seconds, saw two pages or more, or reached a goal.
table.title: Title
table.readDetail: How far down the page was read, on average.
table.exitRateDetail: Visits that ended on the page, of its views.
table.rageDetail: Three clicks or more on the same element within a second.
table.deadDetail: A click after which nothing changed on the page for a second: no new page, no change to the page, no scroll, no field focused.
table.name: Name

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Visits to {{site}} on {{domains}}, with where they came from and what they reached.
overview.againstPrevious_one: Against the day before, in grey. Numbered marks are the team's annotations.
overview.againstPrevious_other: Against the {{count}} days before, in grey. Numbered marks are the team's annotations.
overview.againstYear: Against the same days last year, in grey. Numbered marks are the team's annotations.
overview.marksAreNotes: Numbered marks are the team's annotations.
overview.goalsDetail: Share of visits that reached each

annotations.addDetail: A note on a day of this site's timeline: a launch, a campaign, a holiday, an outage.
annotations.everyone: Everyone who can see this site's reports sees it.

realtime.title: Realtime
realtime.description: The last 30 minutes, as events arrive. A visitor counts as here for 5 minutes after their last event.
realtime.latestPaused: Paused: the list waits until you resume.

acquisition.title: Acquisition
acquisition.channelsDetail: Every visit is put in one channel by its referrer and utm_* parameters, the first rule that matches.
acquisition.sourcesDetail: The site that sent each visit, and the full addresses it came from without their query string.
acquisition.campaignsDetail: The utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term and utm_content of tagged links.
acquisition.assistantsDetail: Visits sent by AI assistants: a link in an answer, or utm_source set by the assistant.
acquisition.channelsTotal: {{visits}} visits. Engaged: stayed longer than 10 seconds, saw two pages or reached a goal; bounce is the rest.
acquisition.channelsNote: The rules are the same for every site; a site can put its own sources in a channel under channels in analytics.yaml, such as a partner's newsletter in Email.
acquisition.sourcesPick: Pick a source for the addresses it linked from.
acquisition.referringDetail: Referring addresses, kept without their query string or fragment.
acquisition.noReferrer: No referring address: utm_source names this source on its links.
acquisition.directDetail: These visits had no referrer: a typed address, a bookmark or an app that sends none.
acquisition.taggedVisits: {{visits}} visits with this parameter; visits without it are left out.
acquisition.noCampaigns: No visit in this period came with {{key}}.
acquisition.campaignsNote: utm_* parameters are kept on the visit and dropped from the page address. gclid, msclkid and other ad click ids mark a visit as paid and are not kept.
acquisition.noAi: No visit from an AI assistant in this period.
acquisition.whatCountsDetail: A visit whose referrer is chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, claude.ai, gemini.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com or another assistant, or whose utm_source names one, as ChatGPT adds to the links it shows. An answer that names the site without a link sends no visit and is not counted.

visitors.title: Visitors
visitors.locationsDetail: Country, region and city, looked up in the install's GeoIP database when a visit starts.
visitors.devicesDetail: Kind of device, screen size, and browser and system with their version.
visitors.languagesDetail: The browser's language and time zone, as the page reports them.
visitors.pickCountry: Pick a country for its regions and cities.
visitors.locationOff: This site keeps no places: location is off in analytics.yaml.
visitors.ipNeverKept: The IP address is never stored
visitors.ipNeverKeptDetail_city: It is looked up in the GeoIP database kept in the install when a visit starts, and dropped: only the country, region and city are kept. No lookup leaves the server.
visitors.ipNeverKeptDetail_region: It is looked up in the GeoIP database kept in the install when a visit starts, and dropped: only the country and region are kept, as location: region in analytics.yaml says. No lookup leaves the server.
visitors.ipNeverKeptDetail_country: It is looked up in the GeoIP database kept in the install when a visit starts, and dropped: only the country is kept, as location: country in analytics.yaml says. No lookup leaves the server.
visitors.ipNeverKeptDetail_off: This site keeps no places at all: location is off in analytics.yaml, so no lookup is made.
visitors.geoOff: Places are off for the install
visitors.geoOffDetail: geoip: off in analytics.yaml, or ANALYTICS_GEOIP=off, turns lookups off: new visits have no place.
visitors.geoError: The GeoIP database could not be loaded
visitors.attributionMiddle: , from the DB-IP Lite city database, licensed under
visitors.screensDetail: The screen in CSS pixels, as the browser reports it.
visitors.devicesNote: Browser and system with their version are read from the user agent when a visit starts; the user agent itself is not kept.

behavior.title: Behavior
behavior.pagesDetail: Each page with its views, the time on it and how far down it was read, and where visits entered and left.
behavior.linksDetail: Clicks on links to other sites and on files the site offers.
behavior.sitesearchDetail: What people looked for in the site's own search.
behavior.notfoundDetail: Pages that answered as not found, and where the links to them are.
behavior.frustrationDetail: Rage clicks and dead clicks: where people click and nothing happens, or click again and again.
behavior.pageviewsInAll_one: {{views}} page view in all; the 50 most viewed pages.
behavior.pageviewsInAll_other: {{views}} page views in all; the 50 most viewed pages.
behavior.entryDetail: The first page of each visit; bounce is the share of those visits that were not engaged.
behavior.exitDetail: The last page of each visit.
behavior.noOutbound: No click on a link to another site in this period.
behavior.linksNote: A click on a link to another site counts as outbound, and on a link to a file ending in {{endings}} as a download; downloads in analytics.yaml changes the list. Query strings are dropped from both.
behavior.linksNoteNoDownloads: A click on a link to another site counts as outbound. Downloads are off for this site: downloads: false in analytics.yaml. Query strings are dropped.
behavior.searchOff: Site search is not set for this site
behavior.searchOffDetail: Name the search page and its query parameter under the site in analytics.yaml.
behavior.searchTermsDetail: Terms are kept in lower case; one that looks like an email address or a phone number is masked.
behavior.searchNote: Read from the {{params}} parameter of {{path}}, as analytics.yaml sets it. Other parameters are dropped.
behavior.searchNoteAnyPage: Read from the {{params}} parameter of any page, as analytics.yaml sets it. Other parameters are dropped.
behavior.notFoundTitle: A page counts as not found when its title is {{title}}, or when it says so itself.
behavior.notFoundMeta: A page counts as not found when it says so: <meta name="analytics" content="404"> or openasy.notFound().
behavior.noneNotFound: No page answered as not found in this period.
behavior.fixOwnLink: The link is on one of the site's own pages: correct it there, or redirect the address to the page it meant.
behavior.fixOtherLink: The link is on another site: a redirect to the page it meant keeps those visitors.
behavior.inVainDetail: Of {{clicks}} clicks in this period, the elements that had a rage or a dead click.
behavior.noFrustration: No rage or dead click in this period.
behavior.frustrationNote: Links and form fields are never dead clicks. Replays opens the recorded visits that viewed the page.
behavior.pathsDetail: Where visits went on from a page, or how they reached it, step by step.
behavior.noResultsNote: A search page that found nothing says so with <meta name="analytics" content="no-results"> or openasy.noResults().

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.goalsDetail: The goals of the sites file, and the share of visits that reached each.
conversions.funnelsDetail: The steps a visit takes, in order, from the sites file. A visit counts at a step once it did every step before.
conversions.formsDetail: Where people start a form, how many send it, and the field they leave it at. Never what they typed.
conversions.attributionDetail: Which channels, sources or campaigns brought the visitors who reached a goal, by three models.

goals.noneDetail: Add goals to the site in analytics.yaml: a page to reach, one of your events, or a file to download.
goals.note: A conversion is a visit that reached the goal, counted once however often it did. Goals are set under the site in analytics.yaml and count past visits too.

funnels.noneDetail: Add funnels to the site in analytics.yaml: two to ten steps, each a page or one of your events.
funnels.barsDetail: Each bar is the visits that reached the step; the gap is where they left.
funnels.bySourceDetail: Conversion from the first step to the last.
funnels.nobody: No visit took the first step in this period.
funnels.note: Funnels are set in analytics.yaml under the site, with a path or an event for each step, and are worked out from the visits already kept: a new funnel shows past visits too.

forms.off: Forms are not reported for this site
forms.offDetail: Set forms: true for the site in analytics.yaml.
forms.noneDetail: A form shows once someone enters one of its fields.
forms.on: On {{page}}. A visit starts the form at its first field and sends it with its submit.
forms.valuesNeverDetail: The script sends a field's name and kind when it is entered and left, and nothing it holds. Fields named like a card number or a password are counted by kind only.

performance.title: Performance
performance.description: Core Web Vitals from real visits: how fast the largest content shows, how fast the page answers, how much it shifts.
performance.off: Web Vitals are not measured on this site
performance.offDetail: Set vitals: true for the site in analytics.yaml; the script then measures each page in the browser.
performance.byDeviceDetail: 75th percentile of each kind of device; pick one to see its pages.
performance.byPageDetail: 75th percentile of each page, the slowest first
performance.note: The script measures each page view in the browser, as web.dev does, and sends the values with the page's leave; the 75th percentile is what search engines judge a page by. Turned on with vitals: true in analytics.yaml.
performance.dailyDetail: 75th percentile of each day, all devices.

visits.title: Visits
visits.description: Every visit, newest first. Open one to see what happened, in order.

visit.title: Visit
visit.notFoundDetail: It may be older than the site keeps visits, or its visitor's data was deleted.
visit.timelineDetail: Everything the visit sent, in order.
visit.deleteDetail: Every visit and event of this visitor on this site is deleted, as a request under GDPR or KVKK asks.
visit.deleteNote: The daily totals stay, because they name nobody. This cannot be undone.

sites.title: Sites
sites.description: The sites this analytics measures. They are set in the sites file, and only there.
sites.lastGoodStays: The last good version stays in use until the file is fixed.
sites.noneDetail: Add a site to the sites file; it is read again within a minute.
sites.scriptDetail: Add it to every page of the site, in the head.
sites.keyMissing: serverKey names {{variable}}, which is not set: events from the site's servers are refused.

file.title: Settings
file.description: What {{file}} sets for each site and for the install.
file.readOnlyDetail: Edit the file and commit it. Analytics reads it again within a minute and says here what it could not apply; until then the last good version stays in use.
file.notAppliedTitle: The file on disk is not applied
file.warnings: To fix, though the file is applied
file.noFile: The file has not been applied yet.
file.locationGroupDetail: The IP address is looked up here when a visit starts and then dropped.
file.geoNever: Never: the file is used as it is

setup.title: Setup
setup.description: Measure a site in two steps: list it in the sites file, then add its script to its pages.
setup.step1: 1. List the site in the sites file
setup.step1Detail: {{path}}, read again within a minute of a change. A file with a mistake leaves the last good one in place.
setup.step2: 2. Add the script to the site's pages
setup.step2Detail: One tag in the head of every page. It is served by this analytics, small, and loads nothing from elsewhere.
setup.step3: 3. Your own events, if you want them
setup.step3Detail: From the page, once the script is loaded.
setup.step4Detail: With the key the site's serverKey names, for what happens out of the browser, such as a payment.
setup.kept1: The value of any form field: the script never reads one.
setup.kept2: Query strings, but for utm_* and the parameters the site lists; emails and tokens in addresses are masked.
setup.kept3: The IP address and the user agent: only the place, the browser, system and kind of device are kept.
setup.kept4: Names, emails and phone numbers: a user id that looks like one is refused.

heatmaps.title: Heatmaps
heatmaps.description: Where people clicked on a page and how far they read it, drawn on the page as it is today.
heatmaps.notLoaded: The page did not load its heatmap
heatmaps.notLoadedDetail: The page needs the site's script, and must allow {{origin}} to frame it: frame-ancestors in its Content-Security-Policy, and no X-Frame-Options DENY.
heatmaps.frameDetail: Shown {{width}} pixels wide. Nothing is recorded while the page is open here.
heatmaps.elementsDetail: Clicks on this page by element.
heatmaps.noClicks: No clicks on this page in this period

replays.title: Replays
replays.description: Recorded visits, newest first: {{sample}}% of visits, kept {{keep}} days, with every form field masked in the browser.
replays.off: Replays are off for this site
replays.offDetail: Set replays for the site in the sites file, with the share of visits to record and how long to keep them.
replays.noneDetail: A replay shows a few seconds after a recorded visit starts.
replays.noneFiltered: No recorded visit matches the filters in this period.

replay.title: Replay
replay.notFoundDetail: It may be older than the site keeps replays, or its visitor's data was deleted.
replay.shortDetail: The visit ended before the page was recorded.
replay.masked: Form fields were masked in the browser, and emails, tokens and keys in the page's text again before the replay was kept.

settings.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this analytics for access.
settings.accountDetail: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.
settings.membersDetail: Who can sign in to this analytics, and with which role. Viewers see every report and visit; editors also add annotations; admins also export and delete a visitor's data, and manage members and tokens.
settings.signinDetail: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.
settings.tokensDetail: For scripts. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.

search.userDetail: Visits of this user id on {{site}}

paths.fromDetail: {{visits}} visits. Each band is the visits that moved from one page to the next; grey ones left the site.
paths.toDetail: {{visits}} visits. Each band is the visits that came from one page to the next; grey ones started their visit there.

attribution.firstDetail: All the credit to the visitor's first visit in the {{days}} days before.
attribution.lastDetail: All of it to the visit that converted. The other reports use this one.
attribution.linearDetail: Shared evenly among every visit in the {{days}} days before, the converting one included.
attribution.title: {{goal}}: {{model}}
attribution.summary_one: {{conversions}} conversion; a median of {{visits}} visits before each, looking back {{days}} days.
attribution.summary_other: {{conversions}} conversions; a median of {{visits}} visits before each, looking back {{days}} days.
attribution.note: Visits are joined by the visitor id the script keeps in the browser; only kept visits count, and on a site with consent, only those after it.

ecommerce.title: Ecommerce
ecommerce.salesDetail: Orders and revenue from the shop's purchase events, and the steps to them.
ecommerce.productsDetail: Each product's views, carts and sales, by SKU.
ecommerce.revenueDetail: Revenue and average order by where the visit that bought came from.
ecommerce.off: Ecommerce is off for this site
ecommerce.offDetail: Name the site's currency and turn on ecommerce in the sites file, then call openasy.ecommerce() on the shop's pages or send the same events from its servers.
ecommerce.funnelDetail: Visits at each step, having done the ones before
ecommerce.sends: openasy.ecommerce("purchase", { order, value, currency, items }) on the thank-you page, or the same event from the shop's server with its serverKey, so ad blockers miss no order. Each order id counts once; a refund names its order. Items carry a SKU, name, category, price and quantity, nothing about who bought.
ecommerce.lastTouch: Credited to the visit that bought (last touch).
ecommerce.attributionNote: Conversions, Attribution compares first touch, last touch and linear for any goal.

retention.title: Retention
retention.cohortsDetail: Of the visitors first seen in a week, the share that came back each week after.
retention.stickinessDetail: Daily, weekly and monthly active visitors, and how many of the month's come on a day.
retention.lifecycleDetail: Each week's visitors as new, returning, or back after four weeks or more away.
retention.note: A visitor is the random id the script keeps in the site's localStorage. Another browser or cleared storage is a new visitor. Weeks start on Monday, in UTC.
retention.weeklyDetail: This week is not over yet, so its column is still filling.
retention.dauMauHint: A content site is usually 2 to 5%
retention.activeDetail: Monthly is hidden at first; its scale hides the other two.
retention.dormantDetail: Came the week before, not this week.
retention.backDetail: Came this week after four weeks or more away.

searchConsole.title: Search
searchConsole.description: What people searched before they came: queries, impressions, clicks, click-through rate and position, from each search engine's own tools.
searchConsole.noneDetail: Name the site's property in each engine under searchConsole in the sites file, and set its key in the install's environment: ANALYTICS_GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, ANALYTICS_BING_API_KEY, ANALYTICS_YANDEX_TOKEN.
searchConsole.keyMissing: {{engine}} is linked, but its key is not set
searchConsole.keyMissingDetail: Set {{variables}} in the install's environment; nothing is imported until then.
searchConsole.imported: Imported daily, up to {{day}}; last asked {{ago}}.
searchConsole.notYet: Imported daily; the first import runs shortly after start.
searchConsole.hidden: {{clicks}} clicks came from queries {{engine}} keeps private, too rare to show.
searchConsole.pagesDetail: Search figures beside what the visits did once they arrived.
searchConsole.bounceHereDetail: From Analytics: visits that entered on the page and left without engaging.
searchConsole.noPagesYandex: Yandex gives queries only, not pages.
searchConsole.note: The engines settle their numbers a few days late, so the last days are imported again. Filters do not apply here: the engines know nothing of the visits.

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.emailDetail: Reports sent by email on a schedule, each with its segment and the sections chosen.
sharing.linksDetail: Read-only dashboards for people without an account: totals only, public or behind a password.
sharing.alertsDetail: Rules that watch traffic for what is unusual, and where they send it.
sharing.noSmtp: No mail server in the sites file
sharing.noSmtpDetail: Email reports and alert emails go out through the mail server named under smtp: in the sites file, with its password in ANALYTICS_SMTP_PASSWORD.
sharing.newReportDetail: Sent on a schedule in the time zone of the sites file, for whole days up to the end of the day before.
sharing.emailNote: A report is an HTML email with the chosen sections and their totals, and their tables as CSV files. Each recipient can stop it from a link in the email.
sharing.name: Name
sharing.every_daily: Every day at 08:00, for the day before
sharing.every_weekly: Mondays at 09:00, for the 7 days before
sharing.every_monthly: The 1st of the month at 09:00, for the 30 days before
sharing.revoked: {{name}} was revoked; the link no longer opens.
sharing.newLinkDetail: Anyone with the link opens these reports of {{site}}, read-only.
sharing.linkOnce: The address is shown only now; Analytics keeps only its hash. Make a new link if it is lost.
sharing.totalsOnlyDetail: A shared link shows the chosen reports of the site, with a period and a comparison. Never a visit, a replay, a heatmap or a visitor id; it filters only by channel, source, campaign, country, device, browser, system, page and goal, and opens at most 120 times a minute.
sharing.rulesDetail: Usual is the median of the same hour of the same weekday over the 8 weeks before.
sharing.ruleDrop: Visits an hour fall below {{share}} of the usual
sharing.ruleSpike: Visits an hour pass {{times}} times the usual
sharing.alertText: {{visits}} visits in the hour, against a usual {{usual}}.
sharing.alertsNote: Checked a few minutes into each hour, for the hour before. A drop needs a usual of 10 visits or more, a spike 10 visits or more; an alert is sent when it starts and marked ended at the first normal hour. A webhook gets a JSON POST.
sharing.newRuleDetail: Compares each hour's visits with the same hour of the week before, and says so when they are far off.
sharing.webhookHint: Optional: an https:// address that gets a JSON POST.

shared.goneDetail: It was revoked, it expired, or it was never made. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
shared.needsPassword: This link asks for its password.
shared.wrongPassword: That is not this link's password.
shared.tooMany: Too many tries; wait a quarter of an hour.
shared.note: Totals only, from OpenAsy Analytics: no visit or visitor is shown here.
